comparison.text: Worst day this season so far: 115 ug/m3 on 2026-08-29. Today is below that. Receipts in the repo.
comparison.caveat: Computed from this project's own logged observations, which start when the project started. Git history is the proof.

comparison.text: That is 1.3x the WHO daily safe limit. The limit is 15. We are not close.
comparison.source_name: WHO, 2021 Global Air Quality Guidelines (PM2.5 24-hour average 15 ug/m3)
comparison.caveat: WHO guidelines are health-based targets, not legal limits. India's own national standard (60 ug/m3 for 24h PM2.5) is four times looser.

comparison.text: If every day were like today, you would live at 6.5x the WHO annual safe level.
comparison.source_name: WHO, 2021 Global Air Quality Guidelines (PM2.5 annual average 5 ug/m3)
comparison.caveat: Compares one day against an annual guideline, so it describes a hypothetical year of days like today, not your actual annual exposure.

comparison.text: A week of air like this = 12 cigarettes. Your lungs are keeping the receipts.
comparison.source_name: Berkeley Earth, Air Pollution and Cigarette Equivalence
comparison.caveat: Extends the Berkeley Earth per-day rule of thumb across a week at the same level. Real weeks vary day to day.

comparison.text: Kids breathe faster than adults, so they absorb more of this per kilo. They also live closer to the ground, where some pollutants peak. WHO's words, not ours.
comparison.source_name: WHO, More than 90% of the world's children breathe toxic air every day (2018)
comparison.caveat: Direct WHO statements: children 'breathe more rapidly than adults and so absorb more pollutants' and 'live closer to the ground, where some pollutants reach peak concentrations'.
